- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, reduce forecast slope; model tends to over-forecast when sentiment is weak.  
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >72.5) with sentiment >0.7, check for overshoot — true price often corrects sharply after spike.  
- When true price drops >5% from recent peak, model often fails to adjust — apply mean reversion bias correction for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and model is flat or slightly rising, consider downward bias — sentiment may be over-optimistic.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if true price deviates >10% from forecast mean after 10–15 days, re-evaluate model’s lag — true price often reacts to sentiment shifts 2–3 days ahead.  
- If sentiment history shows sharp drop (e.g., 0.8 → 0.1) followed by forecast rise, model may be lagging — adjust forecast downward by 1–2 points.
